John / team,

Thanks for the draft language — helpful starting point. A few legal notes from Redwood's side: we want to preserve the commercial intent (i.e., a higher cap overall) while limiting carve-outs that would expand unlimited exposure. Proposed counterpoints below (high level):

  1) Structure: Accept a security incident sub-limit, but set it below the general MSA cap and make it clear whether it is per incident or aggregate. Recommended default: $5,000,000 per incident, aggregated up to $10,000,000 for the term (aligns with finance and our insurance program).
  2) Carve-outs: We will exclude consequential damages broadly, but accept a limited exception where legally required (for example, statutory consumer PII claims). We will also maintain that damages resulting from Redwood's gross negligence or willful misconduct are not capped.
  3) Root cause/attribution: Add a definition in the Security Addendum that limits "security incident" to events caused by Supplier's systems/processes (not customer misconfiguration or third-party services outside Supplier's control). This is important to avoid double-recovery or misattribution.
  4) Insurance and remediation: We can include contractual obligations to maintain cyber insurance at specified limits and explicit remediation obligations (forensic costs, customer notification, credit monitoring) as preferred remedies outside of the cap — but we would expect these to be listed specifically and not all open-ended.

Suggested redline snippet for the Order Form (sample):

  "Notwithstanding anything to the contrary in the Agreement, for claims arising from a Security Incident as defined in the Security Addendum: (i) Supplier's liability shall be limited to the lesser of $5,000,000 per incident and the total fees paid by Customer to Supplier in the twelve (12) months preceding the incident; (ii) aggregate liability for all Security Incidents during the Term shall not exceed $10,000,000; (iii) liability for Supplier's gross negligence or willful misconduct is excluded from these limits; and (iv) consequential damages are disclaimed except where required by applicable law for consumer data protections"

I can prepare a tracked redline that merges John’s suggestions with the language above. If FinTechCo can accept per-incident $5M with a $10M aggregate, that will likely clear internal risk review. If Procurement insists on $7.5M per incident, we'll need to escalate to Finance and discuss higher retention / insurance.
